# Tiny ONNX test fixtures

Three BERT encoders, about 480 KB in total, used by the model-backed integration
tests so that the worker path runs for real in CI (a real ONNX Runtime session,
real tokenizer, real padding and sub-batching) without a multi-gigabyte model.

| dir       | file                   | graph inputs                                  | output                          | loader / env                   |
|-----------|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| `embed/`  | `model.onnx`           | `input_ids`, `attention_mask`, `token_type_ids` | `last_hidden_state [b,s,32]`    | `EMBED_MODELS` (7th field)     |
| `rerank/` | `model_quantized.onnx` | `input_ids`, `attention_mask`                 | `logits [b,1]`                  | `RERANKER_MODELS`              |
| `splade/` | `model.onnx`           | `input_ids`, `attention_mask`                 | `logits [b,s,vocab]` (MLM head) | `SPLADE_MODELS`                |

Each directory has a `tokenizer.json` (WordPiece, ~100 pieces, `[CLS] ... [SEP]`).

## What they are not

The weights are random (fixed seeds) with `initializer_range=0.5`, so outputs
differ per input but carry no meaning. Tests assert shape, determinism,
normalisation, and independence from batch-mates; never relevance or ranking.
Semantic checks need a trained model and stay manual (`tests/rerank_smoke.rs`).

## Provenance and licence

Generated by `scripts/gen_test_fixtures.py` (pinned in
`scripts/test-fixtures.requirements.txt`) from randomly initialised
`transformers` BERT configs. No third-party weights, vocabulary or data are
included, so the files carry the repository's own licence (Apache-2.0 OR MIT).

Why not a published tiny model? The candidates checked
(`sentence-transformers-testing/stsb-bert-tiny-onnx`, 17 MB, no licence declared;
`cross-encoder-testing/reranker-bert-tiny-gooaq-bce-onnx`, 17 MB, Apache-2.0;
`sparse-encoder-testing/splade-bert-tiny-nq-onnx`, 33 MB, Apache-2.0) all export
`token_type_ids`, which the reranker and SPLADE loaders reject (they feed exactly
`input_ids` + `attention_mask`), and are 35x larger than a generated model.

## Integrity

`SHA256SUMS` lists every file; CI checks it before the tests run. ONNX export is
not byte-reproducible across torch versions, so regenerating changes the hashes:
regenerate, commit the new files and `SHA256SUMS` together.

```sh
python3 -m venv /tmp/fx && /tmp/fx/bin/pip install -r scripts/test-fixtures.requirements.txt
/tmp/fx/bin/python -I -B scripts/gen_test_fixtures.py tests/fixtures/tiny
```

## Running the tests

```sh
export ORT_DYLIB_PATH="$(scripts/fetch-ort.sh)"   # pinned ONNX Runtime, sha256-checked
cargo nextest run --locked --test multi_process_e2e --test worker_e5_inference ...
```

Without `ORT_DYLIB_PATH` (or without the fixtures) the tests print `SKIP` and
pass on a developer machine, and **fail when `CI=true`**.
`EMBED_TEST_FIXTURES=<dir>` points the tests at another fixture root.
